slides.heading: The Internet <accent>Noticed.</accent>
slides.caption: 5.2M views. 15K GitHub stars. Addy Osmani called it 'built for humans and agents.'

slides.text:
Google just open-sourced a CLI that lets you control your <accent>entire Google Workspace</accent> from the terminal.

Drive. Gmail. Calendar. Docs. Sheets. Slides.

One command. One tool. <accent>Zero boilerplate.</accent>

slides.heading: What is a <accent>CLI?</accent>
slides.caption: GUI = clicking buttons. CLI = typing commands. Think of it as a text remote control for your computer.

slides.heading: One CLI. <accent>Every</accent> Google Service.
slides.caption: GWS CLI connects Claude Code to Drive, Gmail, Sheets, Docs, Slides, and Calendar through a single interface.

slides.heading: Why <accent>GWS CLI</accent> Changes Everything
slides.caption: One interface. JSON-first. Auto-discovery. Zero maintenance. Built-in skills. Low overhead.

slides.heading: Old Way vs <accent>GWS CLI</accent>
before: API calls with raw markdown output
Manual auth for each Google service
after: One CLI, all services, tiny footprint
Claude Code creates directly in Workspace

slides.heading: What Can <accent>GWS</accent> Do?
slides.caption: Ask Claude Code and it lists every capability: Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and 100+ built-in skills.

slides.heading: 100+ Built-in <accent>Skills</accent>
items: Triage and archive emails by label
Find free time and schedule meetings

slides.heading: Install from <accent>GitHub</accent>
slides.caption: Go to github.com/googleworkspace/cli. Open source, Apache 2.0. One npm install and you're ready.

slides.heading: Or Let <accent>Claude Code</accent> Do It
slides.caption: Paste the GitHub link into Claude Code. Say 'Install this GWS CLI and help me set up everything.' It reads the docs and installs for you.

slides.heading: Configure <accent>GCP Auth</accent>
slides.caption: Once installed, you need to set up Google Cloud authentication. Here's the manual setup (no gcloud needed).

slides.heading: Step 1: Create <accent>GCP Project</accent>
slides.body:
- Go to console.cloud.google.com
- Click 'New Project'
- Name it (e.g. 'Claude Code GWS')
- Wait for it to spin up, then select it

slides.heading: Step 2: <accent>Enable</accent> APIs
slides.body:
- Go to APIs & Services in your project
- Enable each API you want to use:
- Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Sheets, Docs, Slides
- Click the enable link one at a time

slides.heading: Step 3: <accent>OAuth</accent> Consent Screen
slides.body:
- Go to APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen
- Click 'Get Started'
- Choose Internal (your org) or External
- If External: add your email as test user
- Fill in app name and contact info, then create

terminal.text: > User type: Internal (or External + test user)

slides.heading: Step 4: Create <accent>OAuth Client ID</accent>
slides.body:
- Go to APIs & Services > Credentials
- Click 'Create Credentials' > OAuth Client ID
- Application type: Desktop app
- Name it (e.g. 'GWS')
- Download the JSON file

terminal.text: Client ID and Client Secret created

slides.heading: Step 5: Save Credentials & <accent>Login</accent>
slides.body:
- Save the downloaded JSON to ~/.config/gws/
- Rename it to client_secret.json
- Run gws auth login
- Browser opens, choose your account
- Allow access to all services

slides.heading: Step 6: <accent>Verify</accent> It Works
slides.body:
- Run a simple test command
- If you get an API error, click the enable URL
- Wait 10 seconds and retry
- Once it works, you're all set!

terminal.text: Found 5 files in your Google Drive
GWS CLI is ready to use!

slides.heading: Key <accent>Commands</accent> Cheat Sheet
items: gws drive files list -- List your Drive files
gws gmail users messages list -- Read your inbox
gws calendar events list -- View your calendar
gws sheets spreadsheets create -- Create a new sheet
gws auth login --scopes drive,gmail -- Login with specific APIs

slides.text:
This is not another MCP config.
Not another API wrapper.

It's one CLI that gives Claude Code
access to your entire Google Workspace.

Install it today. You'll wonder
how you coded without it.

slides.heading: One <accent>Disclaimer</accent>
slides.caption: This is NOT an officially supported Google enterprise product. It's an open-source CLI still in active development (pre-v1.0). Expect some rough edges. But it will only get better from here.
